Practice SIEM queries, one language at a time
Start with a short guide, try the examples, then compare the same evidence in all four languages.
Splunk SPL · Microsoft Kusto Query Language reference · IBM QRadar AQL · FortiSIEM Advanced Search SQL
What can I practice here?
15 datasets contain 121,606 original records. Each dataset has 10 exercises in each of the four languages: 600 exercise and language combinations. The browser interpreter supports an educational subset; this is not a connection to a production SIEM.
Do I need an account?
No. Run queries and use the cheat sheet without signing in. Google sign-in saves server-verified progress and gives you a public display name on the leaderboard.
Where do the logs come from?
Imported logs come from Security Datasets by OTRF. Source records and the dataset license are available in the playground.

Your investigation workbench
Choose Guided practice for exercises, or Free query to experiment with scratch data or an imported capture. Documentation for the selected language is linked beside the editor; Cheat sheet compares equivalent operations across all four languages.
Select a dataset, exercise, and language, then run your query. Check solution compares your answer on the full capture and two deterministic variations of the same source records.
  1. The 15 datasets contain 121,606 records from your Windows, AWS, and Linux logs. Imported captures contain no synthetic login events. Free query has a separate, explicitly labeled scratch sample.
  2. Guest progress and drafts stay on this device. Sign in with Google to save server-verified progress and join the leaderboard.
  3. Source records preserves the original JSON record or Linux audit line. CSV records preserve original column values as JSON.
This is a local educational interpreter, not the original Splunk, Kusto, Ariel, or FortiSIEM engine. Platform views use an explicit training schema. Missing fields stay empty; no user, host, IP, QID, or timestamp is invented.
Each capture has its own clock: the latest timestamp in that file. Dataset names describe source scenarios; a text match alone does not establish malicious activity.
ZIP archives duplicate extracted logs. __MACOSX files are metadata. The two .pcapng files are listed in the inventory but need packet decoding before SIEM queries.
Imported logs: Security Datasets by Roberto Rodriguez, Jose Luis Rodriguez, and Open Threat Research Forge. Upstream license notice. This independent lab is not affiliated with the SIEM vendors.
